title: Smooth finite type neighbourhood of a field-valued object from deformation axioms
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]: cartesian lifts exist along every base map, and each fibre is a groupoid. Assume its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that for objects $a,b$ over any $S$-scheme $T$, the sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_T(a,b)$ is an algebraic space over $T$. Assume the following five conditions.
(1) For every small directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes $T_i$ with limit $T$, the functor $2\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal X(T_i)\to\mathcal X(T)$ is an equivalence; objects on the left occur at a stage and arrows at sufficiently late common stages.
(2) For every pushout $B'=B\amalg_A A'$ of spectra of Artinian local rings of finite type over $R$, with $A\to A'$ a thickening (a closed immersion defined by a nilpotent ideal), the restriction functor $\mathcal X(B')\to\mathcal X(B)\times_{\mathcal X(A)}\mathcal X(A')$ is an equivalence. A local ring is a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal, and Artinian means its descending chains of ideals stabilize.
(3) For every field $k$ with $R\to k$ of finite type and every $x_0\in\mathcal X(k)$, the tangent space (isomorphism classes of objects over $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with an identified restriction $x_0$) and the infinitesimal automorphism space (automorphisms of the trivial deformation restricting to the identity of $x_0$) are finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces [def-weil-field].
(4) For each complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m)$ with residue field finite type over $R$, every system of objects $x_n\in\mathcal X(A/\mathfrak m^n)$, $n\geq1$, with compatible transition isomorphisms is the restriction, with these isomorphisms, of an object over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].
(5) For every $U$ locally of finite type over $S$ and $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, versality at a finite type point $u\in U$ holds throughout the finite type points of some open neighbourhood of $u$. Here finite type means that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type; versality means that for every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with nilpotent kernel and residue field $\kappa(u)$, every $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and every deformation over $A'$ identified over $A$ with the pulled-back $x$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism with the deformation extending that identification.
Then, for each finite type $R$-field $k$ and each $x_0\in\mathcal X(k)$, there exist an affine scheme $U$ of finite type over $S$, an object $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and a finite type point $u\in U$ with a specified $R$-isomorphism $\kappa(u)\cong k$, such that $x|_u\cong x_0$ and the induced morphism $h_U\to\mathcal X$ is representable by algebraic spaces and smooth. Here $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$ viewed as a discrete groupoid; representability means every $h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_T$ is an algebraic space, and smoothness is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Finite type and locally finite type have the meaning of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 07XY (lemma-get-smooth), specialized to an affine G-ring base; the base local-ring hypothesis follows by localizing the defining G-ring condition, as explained in the opening paragraph of the proof of proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring in more-algebra.tex. An affine neighbourhood of the distinguished point may be chosen after shrinking the finite type scheme in the conclusion.

proof.text: Fix $k$ and $x_0$ as in the conclusion. The G-ring hypothesis includes that $R$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-rs-versal-formal-object] to $\mathcal X,k,x_0$. Its pushout hypothesis is precisely (2), and its tangent hypothesis is the tangent-space clause of (3); the finite infinitesimal-automorphism clause is stronger than this step needs. Obtain a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $(C,\mathfrak m)$ with residue field $k$ and a versal system $(\xi_n)$ with $\xi_1\cong x_0$.

source.place: Tag 07XY (lemma-get-smooth), first three sentences; Tag 07WU and Formal Deformation Theory Tag 06IW

proof.text: Hypothesis (4) makes this particular system effective: choose $x_C$ and transition-compatible isomorphisms $x_C|_{C/\mathfrak m^n}\cong\xi_n$. Let $s$ be the image of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The ring $R_s$ is Noetherian: if $J\subseteq R_s$ has contraction $I\subseteq R$ and $a/t\in J$, then $a/1=(t/1)(a/t)\in J$, so $a\in I$. Thus $J=IR_s$, and finite generators of $I$ generate $J$. It is a G-ring: primes of $R_s$ correspond to primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq s$ of $R$, and $(R_s)_{\mathfrak qR_s}\cong R_{\mathfrak q}$, so their local completion maps are exactly those required by the definition of a G-ring for $R$. This is the localization observation in the opening of More on Algebra Tag 07PV. Hypothesis (1) in particular gives preservation of limits on objects. Thus [lem-sfb-artin-effective-versal-algebraization] applies to the effective versal system. It gives $V,y,v$, an $R$-isomorphism $\kappa(v)\cong k$, versality of $y$ at $v$, and $y|_v\cong\xi_1\cong x_0$.

source.place: Tag 07XY, effectivity and application of lemma-approximate-versal (07XH); more-algebra.tex Tag 07PV, opening of the proof

proof.text: By (5), choose an open $W\subseteq V$ containing $v$ such that $y$ is versal at every finite type point of $W$. Choose a finite-type affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $V/S$ containing $v$. The complement of $W\cap\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $V(I)$ for an ideal $I$; since $v$ is outside $V(I)$, choose $f\in I$ outside its prime. Then $v\in U=D(f)\subseteq W$, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] identifies $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B_f$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate $B/R$, then their images and $f^{-1}$ generate $B_f/R$, so $U$ is affine and of finite type over $S$. Set $x=y|_U$ and $u=v$. Restriction to this open does not change the local ring or residue field at $u$, so the specified $R$-isomorphism $\kappa(u)\cong k$ and $x|_u\cong x_0$ persist. The same generator calculation below shows that $v$ being finite type in $V$ makes $u$ finite type in $U$. A finite type point of $U$ is a finite type point of $W$: on an affine neighbourhood a canonical point map is a map to its residue field. Explicitly, for an affine neighbourhood with ring $A$ and a principal open $D(g)$ through the point, let $K$ be its residue field. If $K=A_g[c_1,\ldots,c_t]$, then $K=A[c_1,\ldots,c_t,\bar g^{-1}]$; conversely any finite set of $A$-algebra generators also generates over $A_g$, since $\bar g$ is already invertible in $K$. Such principal opens form a basis. A point map is quasi-compact, its inverse image of an affine open being empty or a one-point field spectrum. For Artinian local test rings with closed image in $U$, every map to $W$ factors through $U$, since the spectrum has only that one point. Hence versality on $W$ restricts to versality of $x$ at every finite type point of $U$.

source.place: Tag 07XY, shrinking by openness of versality; affine refinement using Morphisms finite type definition and Schemes basic-open localization

proof.text: For an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and $z\in\mathcal X(T)$, put $P=U\times_S T$ with projections $p,q$. By the diagonal hypothesis the sheaf $I=\operatorname{Isom}_P(p^*x,q^*z)$ is an algebraic space over $P$. Its composite map to $T$ represents $h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_T$: on a $T$-scheme $T'$ a point consists exactly of an $S$-map $a:T'\to U$ and an isomorphism $a^*x\cong z|_{T'}$. There are no additional automorphisms because the two represented groupoids $h_U,h_T$ are discrete. Thus the induced morphism $h_U\to\mathcal X$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 07XY, use of the representable diagonal before lemma-implies-smooth; direct description of the represented 2-fibre product

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-artin-versal-field-lifting] to $U,x$. The Rim-Schlessinger hypothesis remains (2), and step 3 gives versality at every finite type point. Consequently for every finite type $R$-field $l$ and every $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}l\to U$, all the Artinian deformation diagrams over $l$ lift with their prescribed isomorphisms. The lemma explicitly includes finite extensions of the residue field of the image point, so this conclusion is about all such $\alpha$, not just canonical residue-field maps.

source.place: Tag 07XY, application of lemma-versal-smooth (07XT), including the residue-field extension in 07XG

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-artin-representable-infinitesimal-smoothness] to $h_U\to\mathcal X$. Its source $U$ is of finite type by step 3, the target preserves directed affine limits by (1), representability is step 4, and the required lifting for all finite type field-valued points is step 5. Hence the morphism is smooth. Together with the affine construction, the preserved residue-field identification and the object isomorphism from step 3, this gives every clause of the conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07XY (lemma-get-smooth), with a principal affine refinement of the neighbourhood
